description: Cross-language fixture corpus for the browser-worker protocol. Valid cases must decode and re-encode to the byte string recorded in canonical.json; invalid cases must be refused with the recorded reason. A fixture is the only place a protocol example is written down. The frame_too_large and payload_too_large reasons are exercised in test/browser-frame.test.ts with values built at run time rather than by a committed fixture, because reaching either bound needs roughly 200 KiB of committed data.

valid.name: worker-register
valid.note: Registration precedes identity assignment, so the envelope carries no worker_id. sandbox_enabled records the docs/SECURITY.md section 10 posture.

valid.name: worker-register-ack
valid.note: Assigns the worker identity and the single project it may accept sessions for.

valid.name: worker-heartbeat
valid.note: Capacity report used to detect a lost worker.

valid.name: worker-heartbeat-ack-revocation
valid.note: The revocation direction of ADR-0026: the answer restates the whole assignment, and an empty list means the worker now serves nothing. A worker that acted on the previous answer stops within one heartbeat interval rather than at its next restart.

valid.name: worker-contexts
valid.note: What the worker is actually holding, which reconciliation compares against control-plane state (docs/OPERATIONS.md section 9).

valid.name: session-allocate
valid.note: Allocation carrying the published-service origin that bounds egress, the route capability the worker presents to the tunnel gateway on requests to that origin, the initial epoch and the worker-enforced session limits. The origin's leftmost label is the service public_alias, never its svc_ identifier.

valid.name: session-allocated
valid.note: READY response recording browser type and version on the session.

valid.name: command-navigate-relative
valid.note: The docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.4 example: a relative URL and a bounded wait condition, with the section 6.4 envelope fields present.

valid.name: command-select-option
valid.note: select_option addresses the element by a reference from the current snapshot, so a stale reference fails rather than selecting whatever now occupies that position.

valid.name: command-press-key
valid.note: A key press with no element reference goes to whatever the page has focused. The key comes from the closed vocabulary of key_name.

valid.name: command-scroll
valid.note: A scroll is a bounded movement in CSS pixels, not a request to reach the end of an infinite list.

valid.name: command-result-snapshot
valid.note: The section 7.4 snapshot shape, labelled untrusted_browser_content with instruction_policy do_not_follow_as_instructions.

valid.name: command-result-screenshot
valid.note: A system capture at the 390x844 preset with device_scale_factor 2, reporting the verified artefact digest and size.

valid.name: command-result-epoch-stale
valid.note: A refusal carries no page-derived content, so it is labelled trusted_control_plane and returns the epoch that is actually current.

valid.name: session-status-failed
valid.note: Crash transition carrying both the previous and the new status, per docs/EVENTS.md section 8.

invalid.name: allocate-capability-too-short
invalid.note: The route capability has the same bounds as the connector protocol gives it, so a value too short to be a real credential is refused by the schema rather than presented to the tunnel gateway.

invalid.name: command-without-control-epoch
invalid.note: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 6.4 makes the control epoch mandatory on every command; the schema, not the worker, is the first thing that refuses its absence.

invalid.name: command-without-controller
invalid.note: A command with no controller identity could not be authorised against a lease.

invalid.name: command-navigate-with-click-params
invalid.note: A command carries only its own parameters, so an unused parameter set cannot ride along.

invalid.name: command-timeout-out-of-range
invalid.note: docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.4 forbids an unbounded wait; a day-long timeout is outside the declared bound.

invalid.name: wait-network-idle-with-selector
invalid.note: Network idleness has no target, so a selector alongside it is a contradiction rather than an ignored field.

invalid.name: navigate-to-non-http-scheme
invalid.note: A navigation target is an http(s) URL or a root-relative path; file: never reaches the browser.

invalid.name: result-trusted-with-snapshot
invalid.note: ADR-0010: page-derived content cannot be returned under a trusted label. The generated validator refuses it on both sides of the channel.

invalid.name: snapshot-text-with-control-characters
invalid.note: A hostile page cannot smuggle terminal escape sequences through a snapshot.

invalid.name: register-with-worker-id
invalid.note: A worker does not assign its own identity; the control plane does.

invalid.name: allocate-unknown-property
invalid.note: Unknown properties are refused, so a request cannot smuggle a sandbox-disabling flag past the schema.

invalid.name: press-key-outside-vocabulary
invalid.note: The key vocabulary is closed. A combination outside it — here the developer-tools shortcut — is refused by the schema rather than passed to Chromium to interpret.

invalid.name: unknown-message-type
invalid.note: An unknown command type is rejected, never ignored: script evaluation is not a version 1 capability.

invalid.name: unknown-protocol-version
invalid.note: Stage 0 pins version 1 and does not best-effort parse a later one.
